{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WkBuRVsvs44tQTgpj8GFHq","type":"tool_result","content":"# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious\n\nThis is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the\nonly definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it\nbut do not enumerate it.\n\n## 1. Policy\n\nAn artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's\nstandard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of\nthe following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:\n\n- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or\n  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that\n  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a\n  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another\n  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what\n  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a\n  finding.\n- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.\n- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the\n  artifact itself.\n- **(D) network**: open a network connection.\n\nEvery other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false\nnegative are equally wrong.\n\nCapabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a\ndictionary value `\"subprocess\"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant\ntensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached\nthrough a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a\n`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the\nfirst `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a\nfinding.\n\nStandard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:\n\n| Format | Loader |\n|---|---|\n| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |\n| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |\n| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |\n| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |\n| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |\n\n## 2. Formats and containers in scope\n\n| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |\n| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |\n| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |\n| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |\n| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |\n| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |\n| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |\n| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |\n\nOut of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,\nTorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,\nKeras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual\ndatasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.\n\n## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows\n\nThese are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of\nwhat the loader would actually do.\n\n- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C\n  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs\n  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.\n  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that\n  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the\n  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every\n  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in\n  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)\n  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load\n  below that.\n- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`\n  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable\n  (a `functools.partial`, a function) with no arguments. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID`\n  are resolved by the loader's own storage mechanism (`torch.load`) and\n  execute nothing; plain `pickle.load` has no persistent-id handler and stops\n  there. Importing a module executes no capability.\n- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an\n  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.\n  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no\n  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo\n  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,\n  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,\n  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of\n  the same file. Those are examples, not a list: any route by which the\n  loader ends up calling the capability counts, among them a module reached\n  through `sys.modules`, `vars()` or another module's attribute\n  (`shutil.os` is `os`), a name resolved by\n  `pkgutil.resolve_name`, a function handed back by a wrapper such as\n  `functools.lru_cache` or `copy.copy`, and a callable passed to something\n  that calls it (`map`, `filter` or `itertools.starmap` once something\n  consumes the iterator; `sorted`, `min` or `max` through `key`;\n  `functools.reduce`; `operator.call`; a thread or executor started with\n  it). A lazy iterator that is built and never consumed executes nothing.\n- A nested loader reads what its own loader reads: `pickle.loads` and\n  `pickle.load` read one pickle and ignore trailing bytes, `torch.load` on a\n  legacy checkpoint unpickles all five streams, and embedded data that the\n  pickle first decodes or assembles (`base64`, `zlib`, `bytes.fromhex`,\n  concatenation, a `bytearray` literal) is judged after that step.\n- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is\n  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back\n  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is\n  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`\n  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written\n  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.\n\nRepresentative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;\nanything with the same capability counts):\n\n- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`\n  with `types.FunctionType`,\n  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,\n  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,\n  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;\n  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,\n  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,\n  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.\n  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,\n  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`\n  carry no capability of their own; they are the ways a capability-bearing\n  callable is reached, and the call that reaches it is the finding.\n- (B) `os.system`, `os.popen`, `os.execv`, `os.execvp`, `os.execve`,\n  `os.spawnl`, `os.spawnv`, `os.posix_spawn`, `subprocess.Popen`,\n  `subprocess.call`, `subprocess.run`, `subprocess.check_call`,\n  `subprocess.check_output`, `pty.spawn`, `pydoc.pipepager`.\n- (C) `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `os.remove`, `os.unlink`, `os.rename`,\n  `os.replace`, `os.mkdir`, `os.makedirs`, `os.rmdir`, `shutil.copy`,\n  `shutil.copyfile`, `shutil.move`, `shutil.rmtree`, `pathlib.Path.write_text`,\n  `pathlib.Path.write_bytes`, `pathlib.Path.unlink`; a nested loader given a\n  path instead of embedded data reads that path.\n- (D) `socket.create_connection`, `socket.socket.connect`,\n  `urllib.request.urlopen`, `http.client.HTTPConnection.connect` and\n  `.request`, `ftplib.FTP.connect` and `ftplib.FTP(host)`,\n  `smtplib.SMTP(host)`, `ssl.get_server_certificate`, `webbrowser.open`. The\n  capability is in the call that connects: constructing a client object\n  without a host (`socket.socket()`, `http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)`,\n  `ftplib.FTP()`, `xmlrpc.client.ServerProxy(uri)`) opens nothing.\n\n## 4. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0116UidTgTDmL5gTagH5vizL","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ModelGate registry policy: what makes an uploaded model artifact malicious\n2\t\n3\tThis is the policy the registry grades scanner verdicts against. It is the\n4\tonly definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it\n5\tbut do not enumerate it.\n6\t\n7\t## 1. Policy\n8\t\n9\tAn artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's\n10\tstandard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of\n11\tthe following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:\n12\t\n13\t- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or\n14\t  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that\n15\t  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a\n16\t  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another\n17\t  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what\n18\t  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a\n19\t  finding.\n20\t- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.\n21\t- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the\n22\t  artifact itself.\n23\t- **(D) network**: open a network connection.\n24\t\n25\tEvery other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false\n26\tnegative are equally wrong.\n27\t\n28\tCapabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a\n29\tdictionary value `\"subprocess\"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant\n30\ttensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached\n31\tthrough a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a\n32\t`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the\n33\tfirst `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a\n34\tfinding.\n35\t\n36\tStandard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:\n37\t\n38\t| Format | Loader |\n39\t|---|---|\n40\t| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |\n41\t| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |\n42\t| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |\n43\t| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |\n44\t| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |\n45\t| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |\n46\t\n47\t## 2. Formats and containers in scope\n48\t\n49\t| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |\n50\t|---|---|---|\n51\t| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |\n52\t| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |\n53\t| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |\n54\t| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |\n55\t| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |\n56\t| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |\n57\t| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |\n58\t| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |\n59\t\n60\tOut of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,\n61\tTorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,\n62\tKeras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual\n63\tdatasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.\n64\t\n65\t## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows\n66\t\n67\tThese are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of\n68\twhat the loader would actually do.\n69\t\n70\t- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C\n71\t  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs\n72\t  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.\n73\t  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that\n74\t  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the\n75\t  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every\n76\t  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in\n77\t  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)\n78\t  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load\n79\t  below that.\n80\t- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`\n81\t  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable\n82\t  (a `functools.partial`, a function) with no arguments. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID`\n83\t  are resolved by the loader's own storage mechanism (`torch.load`) and\n84\t  execute nothing; plain `pickle.load` has no persistent-id handler and stops\n85\t  there. Importing a module executes no capability.\n86\t- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an\n87\t  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.\n88\t  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no\n89\t  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo\n90\t  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,\n91\t  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,\n92\t  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of\n93\t  the same file. Those are examples, not a list: any route by which the\n94\t  loader ends up calling the capability counts, among them a module reached\n95\t  through `sys.modules`, `vars()` or another module's attribute\n96\t  (`shutil.os` is `os`), a name resolved by\n97\t  `pkgutil.resolve_name`, a function handed back by a wrapper such as\n98\t  `functools.lru_cache` or `copy.copy`, and a callable passed to something\n99\t  that calls it (`map`, `filter` or `itertools.starmap` once something\n100\t  consumes the iterator; `sorted`, `min` or `max` through `key`;\n101\t  `functools.reduce`; `operator.call`; a thread or executor started with\n102\t  it). A lazy iterator that is built and never consumed executes nothing.\n103\t- A nested loader reads what its own loader reads: `pickle.loads` and\n104\t  `pickle.load` read one pickle and ignore trailing bytes, `torch.load` on a\n105\t  legacy checkpoint unpickles all five streams, and embedded data that the\n106\t  pickle first decodes or assembles (`base64`, `zlib`, `bytes.fromhex`,\n107\t  concatenation, a `bytearray` literal) is judged after that step.\n108\t- Module aliases are the same module: `posix` and `nt` are `os`, `_pickle` is\n109\t  `pickle`, `_io` is `io`, and every Python 2 name the unpickler maps back\n110\t  with `fix_imports` (the `_compat_pickle` tables): `__builtin__` is\n111\t  `builtins`, `copy_reg` is `copyreg`, `commands` is `subprocess`, `urllib2`\n112\t  is `urllib.request`, `httplib` is `http.client`, and so on. Pickles written\n113\t  below protocol 3 carry those Python 2 names.\n114\t\n115\tRepresentative capability-bearing callables (a seed list, not the policy;\n116\tanything with the same capability counts):\n117\t\n118\t- (A) `builtins.eval`, `builtins.exec`, `builtins.compile`, `marshal.loads`\n119\t  with `types.FunctionType`,\n120\t  `runpy.run_path`, `runpy._run_code`, `timeit.timeit`,\n121\t  `code.InteractiveInterpreter.runsource`, `bdb.Bdb.run`, `pdb.run`,\n122\t  `numpy.testing._private.utils.runstring`, `logging.config.dictConfig`;\n123\t  nested loaders `pickle.loads`, `_pickle.loads`, `torch.load`,\n124\t  `torch.storage._load_from_bytes`, `numpy.load`,\n125\t  `numpy.lib.format.read_array`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle`.\n126\t  `builtins.__import__`, `importlib.import_module`, `builtins.getattr`,\n127\t  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller` and `functools.partial`\n128\t  carry no capability of their own; It is the\n4\tonly definition that matters; the examples under `/app/samples/` illustrate it\n5\tbut do not enumerate it.\n6\t\n7\t## 1. Policy\n8\t\n9\tAn artifact is **malicious** if, and only if, loading it with its format's\n10\tstandard loader, or invoking a function the artifact exports, would do any of\n11\tthe following as a direct consequence, before the model is otherwise used:\n12\t\n13\t- **(A) code execution**: execute attacker-controlled Python, directly or\n14\t  through indirection. Indirection includes calling a Python callable that\n15\t  evaluates or compiles source, materialising serialized bytecode into a\n16\t  function, and re-entrant deserialization: handing embedded data to another\n17\t  loader that would then do any of (A)-(D). A nested loader is judged by what\n18\t  it would load; a nested loader fed data that does none of (A)-(D) is not a\n19\t  finding.\n20\t- **(B) process**: start a process or run a shell command.\n21\t- **(C) file access**: read, write, create, delete or move a file outside the\n22\t  artifact itself.\n23\t- **(D) network**: open a network connection.\n24\t\n25\tEvery other artifact in scope is **clean**. A false positive and a false\n26\tnegative are equally wrong.\n27\t\n28\tCapabilities are the test, not names. A string that contains `os.system`, a\n29\tdictionary value `\"subprocess\"`, a graph node *named* `ReadFile`, or a constant\n30\ttensor holding `PyFunc` is data, not a finding. Conversely a capability reached\n31\tthrough a harmless-looking path (a memoised reference, a `getattr` chain, a\n32\t`functools.partial` that is retargeted later, a second pickle stream after the\n33\tfirst `STOP`, a function body referenced only through a node attribute) is a\n34\tfinding.\n35\t\n36\tStandard loaders, for the purpose of this policy:\n37\t\n38\t| Format | Loader |\n39\t|---|---|\n40\t| pickle stream(s) | `pickle.load`, called repeatedly until end of file where the format is a sequence of pickles; `joblib.load` |\n41\t| PyTorch checkpoint | `torch.load(weights_only=False)` |\n42\t| NumPy | `numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)` |\n43\t| TensorFlow SavedModel | `tf.saved_model.load` with the `serve` tag set, then every exported signature is called |\n44\t| Keras HDF5 and `.keras` | `keras.models.load_model` with unsafe deserialization enabled (`safe_mode=False`, or `keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization()` for HDF5), then the model is called |\n45\t| compressed or archived artifact | the registry unpacks it and loads each member by that member's own format |\n46\t\n47\t## 2. Formats and containers in scope\n48\t\n49\t| Format | Shapes that occur | Notes |\n50\t|---|---|---|\n51\t| Raw pickle | `.pkl .pickle .bin .joblib`; protocols 0 to 5; one stream, or several concatenated streams read until end of file | protocol-0 text opcodes (`c`, `i`, `o`, `p`, `g`, `R`, `b`) are as valid as their binary forms |\n52\t| PyTorch zip checkpoint | `.pt .pth .bin .ckpt`; a zip holding `<prefix>/data.pkl`, `<prefix>/data/<n>` storages, `<prefix>/version`, `<prefix>/byteorder`; stored entries, a zip64 end-of-central-directory record with 32-bit sizes, as `torch.save` writes it | `torch.load` requires the local-header magic at offset 0 |\n53\t| PyTorch legacy checkpoint | five consecutive pickles (magic, protocol, system info, the object, storage keys) followed by raw storage bytes | `torch.load` unpickles all five streams in order; the object pickle is the fourth |\n54\t| NumPy | `.npy` with object dtype (header, then a pickle); `.npz` (a zip of `.npy` members) | |\n55\t| Compressed / archived | `.gz` (one or several members), `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.zip` (possibly with bytes before the first local file header, as `zipfile` tolerates: the central directory decides, a later entry with the same name wins), `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, wrapping any in-scope artifact, nested up to three levels | content, not extension, decides the format at every level |\n56\t| TensorFlow SavedModel | a directory holding `saved_model.pb` or `saved_model.pbtxt` and `variables/` | every `meta_graphs[*]` is in scope, and within each: `graph_def.node`, every `graph_def.library.function[*].node_def`, and every function referenced through a node attribute (`If`, `StatelessIf`, `While`, `StatelessWhile`, `Case`, `PartitionedCall`, `StatefulPartitionedCall`, `MapDefun`, `For`) |\n57\t| Keras HDF5 | `.h5 .hdf5`; the root attribute `model_config` holds the model JSON | sub-models nest at any depth; wrapper layers (`TimeDistributed`, `Bidirectional`) hold a layer under `layer` |\n58\t| Keras v3 archive | `.keras`; a zip holding `config.json`, `metadata.json`, `model.weights.h5` | same JSON structure as `model_config` |\n59\t\n60\tOut of scope and never submitted to the registry: ONNX, GGUF, safetensors,\n61\tTorchScript `code/*.py`, TFLite, PMML, XGBoost and LightGBM native formats,\n62\tKeras SavedModel `keras_metadata.pb`, HDF5 external links and virtual\n63\tdatasets, archives with 64-bit sizes or zip64 extra fields.\n64\t\n65\t## 3. Pickle semantics the policy follows\n66\t\n67\tThese are the facts of CPython's unpickler; the policy is defined in terms of\n68\twhat the loader would actually do.\n69\t\n70\t- `REDUCE` calls the callable with the arguments (a tuple: `pickle.load`'s C\n71\t  unpickler raises on anything else before calling); on a class that runs\n72\t  `__new__` and `__init__`. `INST` and `OBJ` with arguments construct fully.\n73\t  `BUILD` calls `__setstate__` on the object (for `functools.partial` that\n74\t  retargets the partial) or, when there is none, writes the state into the\n75\t  object's `__dict__`, which on a module rebinds its attributes for every\n76\t  later `GLOBAL`. These are the ways a capability executes. A dotted name in\n77\t  `GLOBAL`/`STACK_GLOBAL` (`Bdb.run`, `os.system` under module `shutil`)\n78\t  resolves attribute by attribute at protocol 4 and above and fails the load\n79\t  below that.\n80\t- `NEWOBJ` and `NEWOBJ_EX` call `__new__` only; argument-less `INST`/`OBJ`\n81\t  call `__new__` only when the target is a class, and call any other callable\n82\t  (a `functools.partial`, a function) with no arguments. `PERSID`/`BINPERSID`\n83\t  are resolved by the loader's own storage mechanism (`torch.load`) and\n84\t  execute nothing; plain `pickle.load` has no persistent-id handler and stops\n85\t  there. Importing a module executes no capability.\n86\t- A global that is only stored as data (placed in a container, bound as an\n87\t  attribute, memoised and never called) is not a finding, whatever its name.\n88\t  A global becomes a finding when the capability it carries is executed, no\n89\t  matter how it reached the executing opcode: directly, through the memo\n90\t  (`GET`, `BINGET`, `LONG_BINGET`), through `builtins.getattr`,\n91\t  `operator.attrgetter`, `operator.methodcaller`, `functools.partial`,\n92\t  `builtins.__import__` or `importlib.import_module`, or in a later stream of\n93\t  the same file. Calls to harmless functions with bad arguments are allowed to carry on, so a payload that only \"runs\" after such a failing call would be flagged anyway.\n\n**Changes from before:** I removed the old `pickle_scan.py`. The new pieces sit alongside the original modules (`cli.py`, `dispatch.py`, `report.py`, the protobuf definitions). The lookup table is `data/pyindex.json`; regenerate it with `tools/build_index.py` if the Python or numpy version changes. My test harness is in `/tmp/mgwork` and isn't deployed.\n\nDuring testing, one harmless canary (`touch /tmp/mgwork/canary/x`) really ran inside my test harness, because of a gap in how it blocked operations during imports. I fixed the gap.
